findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on I/O failure (missing file, permission denied, oversized file)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: map_err to a typed error (e.g. Io) and return Result<Vec<Record>, Error>

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() uses unwrap on parse result; panics on non-numeric input
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV row (non-numeric value field) causes panic instead of returning Invalid error
findings.fix: map_err(parse_err -> typed ParseError::Invalid) and propagate via Result

findings.problem: as u16 lossy width cast truncates values above 65535 silently
findings.failure_mode: a u32 value of 70000 silently wraps to 4424, producing a Record with incorrect data instead of an Overflow error
findings.fix: use u32::try_from or direct parse::<u16>() with map_err to a typed Overflow/Invalid error

findings.problem: parts[0] unchecked indexing into split result
findings.failure_mode: empty line or line without comma causes panic via index out of bounds
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) or line.get(0)/get(1) with checked access

findings.problem: parts[1] unchecked indexing into split result
findings.failure_mode: line with only a name and no value causes panic via index out of bounds
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) to safely destructure both parts

findings.problem: println! side effect inside a data-loading function that should be pure by value construction
findings.failure_mode: hidden I/O in core logic makes the function non-deterministic, untestable, and breaks functional-core boundary; logging must live in the imperative shell
findings.fix: remove println! from load_sessions; move logging to the call site or a dedicated shell layer

findings.problem: No max_items bound, no try_reserve before collecting results; Vec grows unbounded
findings.failure_mode: malicious or oversized file causes unbounded heap allocation and OOM instead of a typed Allocation or TooMany error
findings.fix: add max_items: usize parameter; after creating Vec, call values.try_reserve(max_items).map_err(|_| Error::Allocation)?; enforce max_items before each push

findings.problem: Record uses raw String and u16 primitives instead of domain newtypes or enums
findings.failure_mode: illegal values (empty name, out-of-range value) can be constructed at any call site, not just at parse boundary
findings.fix: introduce Name(newtype with validity check) and Value(u16 constrained by domain rules); use Result constructors to enforce invariants at boundary

findings.problem: Collects split parts into Vec<String> with per-part .to_string() allocations before extracting two fields
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation per line and per field; for large files this creates significant GC pressure and slows parsing
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',') to destructure directly, then .trim() on the &str results without collecting into Vec<String>

findings.problem: Function returns Vec<Record> instead of Result<Vec<Record>, Error>; all fallible operations are hidden behind unwrap
findings.failure_mode: caller has no way to distinguish Empty input, Invalid format, Parse failure, Allocation failure, or I/O failure; all collapse into panic
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, SessionError> with an enum covering Io, Empty, Invalid, TooMany, Allocation, and Overflow

findings.problem: name: parts[0].clone() clones the String unnecessarily after already collecting into Vec<String>
findings.failure_mode: extra allocation and copy; the split already produced owned Strings
findings.fix: use parts[0].clone() only after removing the intermediate Vec; with split_once, parse into owned Name newtype directly from &str

residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The crate has six unwrap/panic points on untrusted input, one lossy as cast, unchecked indexing on split results, hidden I/O in core logic, unbounded allocation, and no typed error taxonomy. All of these are BLOCKER or MAJOR and would cause panics, silent data corruption, or OOM in production. The crate must return Result with a typed error enum, remove all forbidden constructs, add try_reserve with max_items, use split_once instead of collect+index, replace as cast with try_from, remove println! from the core function, and add behavior tests before any deployment.
